title: Filing a late or incomplete incident report is itself a separate Prime Spell Security Incident
content:
After an incident, A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.4.1.1 provides that "unreasonable delay in submitting the Report, or failure to thoroughly and accurately complete it (including omission of relevant facts), as determined by the Core Council, constitutes a **separate** Prime Spell Security Incident and may result in additional penalties."

The move is recursive: the obligation to document a violation is enforced by the same machinery as the violation itself. There is no need for a distinct reporting-compliance regime, because incomplete reporting simply re-enters the incident pipeline — which in turn requires its own report.

The incentive effect is the point. Without this clause a Prime facing a penalty compares the cost of disclosure against the chance of non-detection, and partial disclosure dominates: it looks cooperative while withholding the damaging facts. With the clause, partial disclosure is not a middle path — it is a second offence, and one that A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.4.2.3.2 can then treat as a repeat pattern with an escalation multiplier.

The cost of the design is that "thoroughly and accurately" and "unreasonable delay" are judged by the Core Council with no stated standard, so the clause also widens the discretionary surface documented at A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.3.3.
description: A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.4.1.1 makes the reporting duty self-enforcing: omitting relevant facts is a fresh, independently punishable violation, so concealment costs more than the original breach.
